evidence: src/business/services/MileageService.ts: constructor(private readonly prisma: PrismaService) injects the persistence abstraction
src/business/services/MileageService.ts averageDaily: `const prisma = new PrismaClient();` followed by `prisma.mileage.findMany({ where: { plate } })` skips the injected PrismaService
src/business/services/MileageService.ts record: `this.prisma.mileage.create(...)` uses the injected service, so the same class reaches persistence in two different ways

src/business/services/MaintenanceService.ts: reaches storage only through the injected VehicleTable/WorkOrderTable (`this.vehicles.row`, `this.orders.write`, `this.orders.insert`), unlike MileageService's raw Prisma access
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
Both services handle the fleet workshop: work orders and mileage. They do not use the module's persistence abstractions the same way. MaintenanceService reaches storage only through the injected VehicleTable and WorkOrderTable abstractions. MileageService receives a PrismaService through its constructor and uses it in record(). But in averageDaily() it creates its own `new PrismaClient()` and queries `prisma.mileage.findMany` directly. That skips the injected persistence abstraction, which matches the rubric's fail condition for direct ORM access where the module's own abstraction exists.

Candidate flags:
- Line 14 (`new PrismaClient`), flagged as repo-bypass and service-direct-orm: confirmed.
- Line 15 (`findMany`): this call runs on the client created on line 14, so it is part of the same bypass, not a separate one.
- Line 9 (`this.prisma.mileage.create`): this goes through the injected PrismaService, so it is not a bypass under this rule. It only shows that MileageService works with raw ORM objects while MaintenanceService uses Table abstractions.

I found no proven copied rule: SERVICE_INTERVAL_KM is imported from one shared definition. The 0–40 hour estimate check in MaintenanceService.open may also exist in WorkOrder, but that file is not in the material, so I am not reporting it.

violations.message: MileageService.averageDaily creates its own `new PrismaClient()` and calls `mileage.findMany` directly. This skips the injected PrismaService that the class already holds, so the method reaches the database around the module's own persistence abstraction.

Inconsistent abstraction: MileageService accesses data through raw Prisma (`this.prisma.mileage.create`, PrismaClient). MaintenanceService in the same module uses only the VehicleTable/WorkOrderTable abstractions.
